caption:
Sometimes I pause and ask myself—how did we get here so fast? It feels like just yesterday I was navigating the haze of postpartum, learning how to be a mother while holding tiny hands. The days were long, the nights even longer, and yet somehow, in the blink of an eye… time carried us forward.

Now I look around, and there they are—3 and 5 years old. No longer babies, but little people with thoughts, personalities, and words that surprise me every day. I still see traces of the babies they were in the curve of their cheeks or the way they reach for me when they’re tired. But I also see who they’re becoming—brave, curious, and full of light.

It’s bittersweet, this parenthood journey. The milestones pass quickly, often without fanfare. You don’t always realize the last time is the last time until it’s long gone. But in their growing, I’ve grown too. In their wonder, I’ve found parts of myself I never knew existed.

So yes, time is moving fast—faster than I ever expected—but it’s also carrying us somewhere beautiful. And in the quiet moments, when I let myself feel the fullness of it all, I’m just so grateful to be here, witnessing it.

2025 - 2022

caption:
48 hours in Barcelona… with kids

Stay

Sir Victor: @sirhotels Modern and luxurious accommodation located in the heart of the city. Some of the popular tourist attractions near the hotel include Casa Milà, Casa Batlló, and the Sagrada Familia.

Eat

El Nacional: This multi-space restaurant offers different areas where you can enjoy different types of Spanish food, from tapas to seafood to meats.

Brunch & Cake: This family-friendly place is perfect for brunch, offering a variety of cakes, pastries, and other breakfast items. It’s located in the heart of Barcelona, making it a convenient stop for tourists.

La Boqueria Market: This famous market is not only a place to buy food but also has several bars where you can eat freshly prepared tapas and meals.

Do:

Visit Sagrada Familia: This iconic basilica is one of the most famous landmarks in Barcelona, known for its unique architecture by Antoni Gaudí.

Stroll in Park Güell: Another masterpiece by Gaudí, this park offers beautiful city views, colorful mosaics, and serene green spaces. Make sure you prebook tickets!

Explore Barri Gòtic (Gothic Quarter): Wind your way through the narrow medieval streets of this district, which is full of history, charm, and mystery.

Enjoy the Beach: Barcelona has several beautiful beaches, including Barceloneta Beach, where you can relax, swim, and enjoy the sun.

Walk on Las Ramblas: This bustling street is filled with shops, cafes, and street performers.

Explore the Casa Batlló: This is another one of Gaudí’s masterpieces, known for its unique design and colorful mosaic work.

Parc de la Ciutadella: a park in the city of Barcelona. The park is home to the city’s zoo, the Parliament of Catalonia, a large lake, museums, and a massive fountain

caption:
20 years together. And no, it hasn’t been 20 years of butterflies.

Long term relationships aren’t all romance and highlight reels.
They’re roommate phases.
They’re bickering over dishes and big life decisions.
They’re seasons of distance.
They’re choosing each other when it would be easier to protect your ego.

But they’re also laughter that feels like home.
History no one else understands.
Growing up together… not just growing older.

Healthy marriage isn’t about never struggling.
It’s about learning how to stay.
How to repair.
How to keep choosing the same person in different seasons of life.

If you’re in the messy middle of a long term relationship, you’re not failing. You’re building.

Save this for the days it feels harder than it should.

caption:
13 seconds in Sint Maarten 🌊 SAVE for your next trip

Our time in Sint Maarten has come to an end and to say we are sad about it is an understatement. We had the most beautiful week in this vibrant country. We can’t wait to get back there.

Tips:

- Rent a car! 1. There is so much to see and do 2. Cabs can be super expensive

- Have cash. Although cards are accepted at most places, there will be the occasion you need some good ol’ cash. USD is accepted everywhere 

- Take a day trip by ferry to one of the surrounding islands, like Anguilla, St. Barts. Don’t forget your passport!

- Have dinner in Grand Case, it’s such a fun area filled with luxury restaurants and local spots. There’s even nightclubs if you want to shake your booty

- Head to Marigot to try one of their many French bakeries (this would be good to do when you’re taking ferry somewhere as it’s the same place you’ll catch the ferry from).

- If you’re accommodations isn’t on the beach, rent some beach chairs from one of the many beach clubs on Orient Bay and relax the day away.

POV: You’re having a conflict resolution in front of your children

Fostering a healthy home environment isn’t always about hiding the storms, it’s about teaching how to dance in the rain. 

Just because you have kids doesn’t mean you become immune to arguments, what matters is how you handle these arguments.

Something we’ve had to take a hard look in the mirror and work tirelessly to adjust. 

See, when we resolve conflicts with our partners in front of our children, we are not showing them a world of discord, but a realm of resolution, understanding, and respect. 

It’s important for them to witness disagreements, but more importantly, they need to witness the resolution. 

We are their first teachers, their role models, and their heart’s first home. 

Let’s normalize healthy communication and conflict resolution for the little eyes watching us. Let’s teach them love, not through perfection, but through patience, understanding, and compromise.

caption:
For millions of couples, infertility can be one of the most frustrating and isolating experiences. This is something we know all too well.

Drowning in appointments, fears, and tears I didn’t know which way to turn. Who to ask for help. I had to be strong for my partner, but I was crumbling inside. I felt broken, ashamed.

Causes of male factor infertility are often unclear, it can be hard to know what to do, who to turn to for advice and who you can trust. 

I didn’t know that we were a part of the 15% of Canadian couples that would struggle to conceive. I didn’t know that we weren’t alone in our feelings.

I want you to know you’re not alone either. 

Male factor infertility affects millions of couples worldwide, yet it remains a taboo topic that is often overlooked. From low sperm count to abnormal morphology, there are various reasons why male factor infertility occurs. But with advancements in medical technology and fertility treatments, there is hope for couples struggling with male factor infertility. It's important to break the silence surrounding male infertility and bring awareness to the issue. 

Remember, infertility doesn't define you or your worth as a person or partner.
